body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-DRAIN2-PH-05` (pool: devin), single commit on base `e78f74b1f`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-DRAIN2-PH-05

## Summary

Drain pass over six conflicting bridge PRs in ashlrai/phantom. Five are
superseded — their intent already landed on main through later reconcile /
drain PRs — so they were closed out with no rework. PR 3612 was ~95%
superseded; its only unlanded piece, the `fleet_job_current_batch` fleet MCP
tool, was ported onto current main and tested. One pre-existing stale test
assertion (hardcoded MCP tool inventory in `phx-mcp-host-runs-31r9`) was
repaired in passing.

## Per-PR outcomes

REWORKS_PR: 3667 — SUPERSEDED. Intent (retry failed/not-started targets from
an await-batch report under a fresh deadline) is covered on main by
`ci-receipt-batch-replan` (#3666, landed 7 min before this PR opened) piped
into `ci-receipt-await-batch`. The PR's fused `ci-receipt-retry-batch` verb is
redundant, re-implements report parsing with weaker validation (dead
`parseCiResumePrior` import, speculative `retryRevision`/`emittedAt`/`note`
fields the real report never emits, silent dedup where the shared parser
rejects), and lacks `--target-timeout-ms`/`--ndjson`. Not ported.

REWORKS_PR: 3663 — SUPERSEDED. `--target-timeout-ms` per-target bound is on
main in `src/cli/fleet-ci-receipt-await-batch.ts` and
`src/core/fleet/ci-receipt-await-batch.ts` (`targetTimeoutMs` option,
`Math.min(targetTimeoutMs, remaining)` per wait), landed via reconcile PR
#3713 which also carried this PR's own test file
(`test/fleet-ci-receipt-batch-slice-05ssm1.test.ts`).

REWORKS_PR: 3650 — SUPERSEDED. `fleet ci-resume-plan` on main already accepts
`--artifact-name NAME [--await-ms N [--poll-ms N]]` alongside `--artifact-id`
(landed via #3649, preserved/evolved via #3724): mutually exclusive
acquisition modes, bounded `awaitCiReceipt` wait, plus a newer
`discoverCiReceiptPrior` single-shot path when `--await-ms` is omitted — a
strict superset of this PR's mandatory-await variant.

REWORKS_PR: 3636 — SUPERSEDED. All three pieces are on main:
`fleet_ci_resume_inputs` and `fleet_release_candidate` tools in
`src/mcp/fleet-server.ts` with their modules
(`src/mcp/fleet-ci-resume-inputs.ts`, `src/mcp/fleet-release-candidate.ts`)
and tests, plus the `ci-resume-inputs --stdin` envelope mode in
`src/cli/fleet-ci-resume-inputs.ts` (with the later real-stdin-pipe fix
#3637). Identical test files exist: `test/mcp/fleet-release-candidate-05srm1`,
`test/mcp/fleet-ci-resume-inputs-05srj1`, `test/fleet-ci-resume-stdin-05srl2`.

REWORKS_PR: 3620 — SUPERSEDED. `fleet_email_outbox_batch_await` is on main:
`src/mcp/fleet-email-outbox-batch-await.ts`, full registration in
`src/mcp/fleet-server.ts`, the tool name in `test/support/fleet-mcp-tools.ts`,
and `test/mcp/fleet-email-outbox-batch-await-05srd1.test.ts` (landed via
#3876 RQ-DRAIN-PH-001).

REWORKS_PR: 3612 — REWORKED (partial). Everything except one tool was already
on main byte-identical: `job-history-await`, `path-cochanges` (core+CLI),
`cos/bus-notice`, `fleet-job-history-batch` CLI changes, `fleet-cos-work`,
`friction-seed.json` and all four test files — and main's
`fleet-path-cochanges` CLI is strictly newer (`--stdin` mode). The PR's
stray `src/mcp/fleet-server.ts.orig` merge artifact was dropped. Ported the
sole missing piece: the `fleet_job_current_batch` fleet MCP tool —
`src/mcp/fleet-job-current-batch.ts` (arg validation + sanitized read over
the shared `jobCurrentBatch` core reader, imports adapted to current module
layout: `JOB_CURRENT_PATH_BOUND` now lives in `job-current.js`), server
registration in `src/mcp/fleet-server.ts`, the name in
`test/support/fleet-mcp-tools.ts`, a dispatch/validation case in
`test/mcp/fleet-server.test.ts`, and a dedicated suite
`test/mcp/fleet-job-current-batch-04sqa1.test.ts` (24 tests). Also repaired
`test/phx-mcp-host-runs-31r9.test.ts`'s hardcoded tools/list expectation,
which was already failing on main (missing `fleet_email_outbox_batch_await`,
`fleet_release_candidate`) and now includes `fleet_job_current_batch`.

## Commands run

- `git fetch origin refs/pull/{3667,3663,3650,3636,3620,3612}/head` — PR heads
- `git diff`/`git log`/`git show` per PR vs merge-base and vs `origin/master`
  (superseded checks; unauthenticated GitHub API used only for PR metadata —
  `gh` config is sandbox-blocked)
- `npm run install:worktree` — healed incomplete eslint install
- `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit` — PASS (backend typecheck, clean)
- `npx --no-install eslint <6 changed files>` — PASS (0 errors, 0 warnings)
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — PASS all phases (file selection, fleet
  registry skip, eslint changed files, tsgo --noEmit, realio lane lint,
  verse sync-I/O lint, dedupe recorded)
- `npm run check:docs` — PASS (0 errors)
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- <files>`:
  - test/mcp/fleet-job-current-batch-04sqa1.test.ts — 24/24 PASS
  - test/mcp/fleet-server.test.ts — 20/20 PASS
  - test/phx-mcp-host-runs-31r9.test.ts — 10/10 PASS (was 1 failing before fix)
  - test/mcp/fleet-job-current-04-spw1.test.ts, test/mcp/fleet-job-history-batch-04-spr1.test.ts,
    test/fleet-job-current-batch-04-spx1.test.ts, test/mcp-durable-inbox-recut-31.test.ts,
    test/mcp-fleet-lanes-31.test.ts, test/fleet-mcp-bus-observation-oct31.test.ts,
    test/phx-fleet-mcp-onramp-31s7.test.ts — all PASS
  - Totals: 12 files run, 183 tests, 183 pass / 0 fail (one intermediate
    assertion fix during development, then green)

## Files changed (net +281 / -2 LOC)

- `src/mcp/fleet-job-current-batch.ts` — new, +86
- `test/mcp/fleet-job-current-batch-04sqa1.test.ts` — new, +161
- `src/mcp/fleet-server.ts` — +23/-1 (import, FleetReaders field, tool def,
  name chain, parse, validation, dispatch)
- `test/mcp/fleet-server.test.ts` — +11
- `test/support/fleet-mcp-tools.ts` — +1
- `test/phx-mcp-host-runs-31r9.test.ts` — +1/-1 (stale inventory repair)

## Notes / limitations

- `gh` CLI cannot read `~/.config/gh` under this sandbox; PR metadata was
  fetched via the unauthenticated GitHub REST API (repo is public) and PR
  heads via `refs/pull/N/head`. Rate limit (60/hr shared IP) was exhausted
  mid-task; all needed metadata was collected beforehand.
- Sibling drain branch `codex-bridge/RQ-DRAIN-PH-004` (local, unpushed)
  contains a parallel `fleet_job_current_batch` port with identical
  placement; whichever lands second will see a small textual conflict in
  `fleet-server.ts`/`fleet-mcp-tools.ts` — semantically identical either way.
- No commits made; all changes left uncommitted in the worktree per
  boundary. `.github/` untouched. No secrets printed.
</details>

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-DAILYCIFIX01
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-DAILYCIFIX01` (pool: devin), single commit on base `099289922`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-DAILYCIFIX01

Daily-CI repair, Nov 1 order. Scheduled CI run on `master` (`ci.yml`, cron `3 9 * * *`)
failed Oct 29, 30, 31. This pass covers the **Oct 31 run 41212910266** at SHA
`87273df901278208a55ce5290bd1562aace244bd`. Worktree is at `origin/master`
`e0f429f3f` (post-run); every fix below lands on current master, so both the
historical failure and the still-red parts of it are addressed.

`gh` credential access is blocked on this host (macOS TCC), so remote per-step
logs were unavailable; each failure was reproduced locally at the run SHA and at
HEAD against the exact script the workflow step calls.

## Failing steps and what was done

### 1. "Check publication contracts (hermetic)" — ubuntu authority 1/3 → `npm run check:release`

The step runs 14 test files serially. At the run SHA, three deterministic
source-side failures (plus the out-of-scope owner drift below):

**a) `test/sidecar-literal-imports-315.test.ts` — 30 s timeout, not an offender.**
Decisive evidence: `Error: Test timed out in 30000ms` on
`no runtime source loads a computed specifier outside the documented exceptions`.
The test AST-parses every runtime source (`src/core` + `src/cli` = 1709 files
now); the unfiltered parse outgrew the 30 s budget on a 2-vCPU runner.
Additionally, at HEAD the same test has a real offender — `src/cli/fleet.ts:2554`
`loaded = await import(resolved.module)` — a computed specifier that cannot be
bundled into the compiled sidecar (introduced by `dae38c324` on Nov 1, i.e. it
still fails the check on current master even though it post-dates the run SHA).

Fix:
- `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` (new): each convention verb gets one
  literal `import('./fleet-<name>.js')` loader in `FLEET_SUBCOMMAND_LOADERS`.
- `src/cli/fleet.ts`: convention dispatch now calls `FLEET_SUBCOMMAND_LOADERS[sub]()`
  instead of `import(resolved.module)`; same fallback semantics (module-not-found
  still falls through to the built-in switch). No computed dynamic import remains.
- `test/helpers/sidecar-ast-gate.ts` (new) + `test/sidecar-literal-imports-315.test.ts`:
  a linear character-scan gate (`hasComputedImportCandidate`) decides whether a
  file can contain a non-literal `import(` at all; only the ~45 flagged files
  get the AST pass. The assertion itself is unchanged — every `import(x)` whose
  argument is not a string literal outside the two documented exceptions still
  fails.
  Proof: `npm run test:ci -- test/sidecar-literal-imports-315.test.ts` — before
  fix, timeout at 30 s (exit 1); after, 11/11 pass in ~17–20 s (exit 0) on this
  heavily loaded box; on CI's clean runner it is well inside the budget.

**b) `test/cli-registry-drift.test.ts` — `completions.ts TOP_LEVEL_COMMANDS is missing: top`.**
`src/cli/index.ts` dispatches `case 'top':` (`src/cli/top.ts` exists and exports
`cmdTop`) but the completions list was never updated.
Fix: `src/cli/completions.ts` adds `'top'` to `TOP_LEVEL_COMMANDS`.
Proof: `npm run test:ci -- test/cli-registry-drift.test.ts` — before, exit 1 on
that assertion; after, 5/5 pass (exit 0).

**c) `test/documentation-navigation.test.ts` — packaged-nav ENOENTs.**
See Owner-only below; the fix requires `docs/README.md` / `package.json`, both
off-limits for this pass.

### 2. "Build" — Mac exhaustive (1/4) and Mac exhaustive (isolated) → `npm run build`

Cause at run SHA: the release-dependency-inventory step
(`scripts/build-release-dependency-inventory.mjs`) throws
`release package files declaration is not portable` — run-SHA `package.json`
`files` declared `docs/FLEET-API.md` and `docs/QUARANTINE-LEDGER.md` while the
reviewed `allowedFiles` set in
`src/core/daemon/runtime-release-dependency-inventory.ts` lacked them
(regression introduced Oct 31, same day as the run).
Proof at run SHA: invoking the portability check on the run-SHA manifest throws
exactly that error; at HEAD it passes — the allowlist regression was already
fixed by `ca214b9e4` ("Package files allowlist regression", merged Oct 31 after
the run SHA). Verified: `npm run build` on this worktree passes `check:version`,
`tsc`, `authority-surface`, `copy-assets`, `build-preparation-builtin`, and the
full `vite build` before reaching the inventory step.

### 3. "Build hardened inventory" — Windows service authority → `npm run build`

Same `npm run build` chain, same step, same allowlist failure as (2). Nothing
Windows-specific in the failure — the inventory's Windows custody handling
(homedir selection, chmod-before-unlink, reparse checks) was audited and is not
implicated. Already fixed by `ca214b9e4` at HEAD.

### 4. Merge Gate — sum of the above only.

## Additional source fixes landed in this pass

- **`fleet lane-models` dead dispatch** (`src/cli/fleet.ts`): `lane-models` is in
  `FLEET_VERB_OPTIONS` (which skips the convention fallback) but had no switch
  case, so the verb fell through to `unknown fleet subcommand`. Added the
  `case 'lane-models'` lazy literal import. Verified end-to-end:
  `node dist/cli/index.js fleet lane-models --json` →
  `{"schema":"fleet.lane-models.v1",...}`, exit 0.
- **`src/web-ui/tsconfig.minimal.tsbuildinfo` deleted**: tracked 48 KB incremental
  build artifact committed accidentally by `455f74b84`; no tsconfig or script
  references `tsconfig.minimal` anywhere (repo-wide search), and real build-info
  files live under `node_modules/.cache/` since the incremental-config change.
  Dead code removal in the touched area.

## Owner-only (cannot be fixed without owner-reviewed files)

1. **Packaged documentation index (`docs/README.md` + `package.json`).**
   `test/documentation-navigation.test.ts` fails at HEAD (7 tests; 3 deterministic):
   - `expected [...] to include 'docs/FLEET-API.md'` — `ca214b9e4` removed
     `docs/FLEET-API.md` from `files` to satisfy the allowlist, but
     `OPERATOR_DOCUMENTATION` in `scripts/check-documentation.mjs` still lists it
     as a required operator entrypoint.
   - Packaged-nav ENOENTs — `docs/README.md` holds ~60 relative links to docs not
     in the package payload (at run SHA: `DRIVER.md`, `GRAPH-HTTP.md`,
     `ECOSYSTEM-RELEASE-CONTRACTS.md`, `GROK-ULTRA-RUNWAY.md`; the unshipped set
     grew to ~60 at HEAD after `FLEET-API`/`QUARANTINE-LEDGER` were dropped from
     `files`).
   Minimal owner change: in `docs/README.md`, convert every relative link that
   targets an unshipped doc to the established source-only form
   `https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/<NAME>.md` (the checker
   skips these in package mode — `MODEL-INVENTORY.md` and ~20 others already use
   it). Then for `docs/FLEET-API.md` either (a) restore it to `package.json`
   `files` and to `allowedFiles` in
   `src/core/daemon/runtime-release-dependency-inventory.ts` if it should ship
   (it is a listed operator entrypoint), or (b) remove it from
   `OPERATOR_DOCUMENTATION`. A candidate patch for (a)'s allowlist side exists in
   this worktree's investigation; docs/package manifest are the owner's call.

2. **Generated authority ownership drift** (explicitly out of scope, unchanged):
   `authority-codeowners-310b` and `authority-tier1-closure-310b` still fail at
   HEAD — new Tier-1 roots `src/core/routing/arms.ts`, `src/core/routing/bandit.ts`
   etc. Owner regenerates with `ASHLR_UPDATE_CODEOWNERS=1` /
   `ASHLR_UPDATE_TIER1_CLOSURE=1`. Untouched by this diff.

## Verification

Commands run (all with a temporary `HOME` for test runs):

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `npm run test:ci -- test/sidecar-literal-imports-315.test.ts` | exit 1 (30 s timeout) | exit 0, 11/11 in ~17–20 s |
| `npm run test:ci -- test/cli-registry-drift.test.ts` | exit 1 (`missing: top`) | exit 0, 5/5 |
| `npm run test:ci -- test/daily-ci-fix-nov01.test.ts test/sidecar-literal-imports-315.test.ts test/cli-registry-drift.test.ts test/fleet-subcommand-fallback-31.test.ts test/fleet-verb-convention.test.ts` | n/a (new) | exit 0, 56/56 after fixes |
| `npm run check:release` (the step's own script) | exit 1 | exit 1 — remaining red is owner-only doc-nav + owner-generated drift + load-timeout flakes (below) |
| `npm run build` | exit 1 at run SHA (`release package files declaration is not portable`, proven via the contract check) | passes version-check/tsc/authority/copy-assets/vite; local run cannot complete the inventory step on this host — see Limitations |
| `node dist/cli/index.js fleet lane-models --json` | `unknown fleet subcommand`, exit 2 | `{"schema":"fleet.lane-models.v1",...}`, exit 0 |
| `node dist/cli/index.js fleet lane-truth --json` | n/a (computed import path in source build; convention verbs were dark in the compiled sidecar) | `{"schema":"fleet.lane-truth.v1","lanes":[]}`, exit 0 via literal registry |
| `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` (once, foreground) | — | PASS file selection, PASS eslint changed files, PASS tsc --noEmit, FAIL web typecheck, FAIL realio lane lint, PASS verse sync-I/O lint |

`verify-changed` FAILs are **pre-existing, not caused by this diff**: the realio
lint flags ~60 untouched test files plus two stale allowlist entries
(`test/affected-map-audit.test.ts`, `test/m30.merge-queue-reaper.test.ts`), none
added here; `tsc -p src/web-ui/tsconfig.json` compiles only `src/web-ui/`
sources, none modified (the deleted `.tsbuildinfo` is unreferenced output, and
the web tsconfig's own `tsBuildInfoFile` lives under `node_modules/.cache/`).

## New regression coverage

`test/daily-ci-fix-nov01.test.ts` (hermetic — repository sources only, no
network, no `gh`, no `HOME` use):

body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-BUSFOLLOWSTREAM01SOLH2` (pool: devin), single commit on base `d06564046`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-BUSFOLLOWSTREAM01SOLH2

## Summary

New convention-dispatched fleet verb `ashlr fleet bus-follow` that lets an agent stay
subscribed to local shared bus state as a bounded, resumable JSONL stream, instead of
repeatedly launching snapshot commands (`bus-thread`, `bus-request`).

- `src/core/fleet/bus-follow-stream.ts` — `followBusStream(request, deps)` polls
  `listBusInboxAfter` under a monotonic `performance.now()` deadline (mandatory
  `--duration-ms` 1..3600000). It emits `{type:'message',cursor,receivedAt,envelope}`
  for each live retained receipt (optionally exact `--to` filtered) and
  `{type:'checkpoint',cursor}` as the scan position advances — including past filtered
  and expired rows (sparse cursors). Every emit is awaited, so a checkpoint is only
  offered after all preceding records were accepted by the output stream, and the
  returned cursor is always a safe at-least-once resume point. `retryable` pages
  retry within the deadline; `unavailable`/`invalid`/malformed pages fail closed as
  `source-unavailable` with no falsely advanced checkpoint. AbortSignal ends
  promptly; a final checkpoint is emitted on ordinary duration expiry.
- `src/cli/fleet-bus-follow.ts` — `cmdFleetBusFollow`: strict flag parsing
  (`--after` + `--duration-ms` required; `--to`, `--interval-ms` 100..60000 default
  250, `--root` absolute, `--json` required), SIGINT/SIGTERM wired to an
  AbortController with listener cleanup in `finally`, per-record scrubbing through
  `sanitizePublicJson` plus secret-key `redactFields`, and stdout backpressure via
  the write callback + `'error'` listener (same pattern as `comms-bus.ts` `deliver`).
  Exit codes: 0 expired/cancelled, 1 source/output failure, 2 invalid arguments.
- `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` — regenerated via
  `node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs` (the documented "run it after adding a verb"
  step). Adds `'bus-follow'` plus three entries for verbs that had already landed on
  master unregistered (`bus-scatter`, `graph-observe`, `graph-context-run`): the
  committed `test/fleet-subcommand-registry.test.ts` sync check was already failing
  on master, and only a full regeneration makes it pass with the new file present.

Read-only throughout: never creates or mutates inbox files, never executes bodies,
never dispatches workers; `--root` only selects an existing local store; routing
labels are untrusted data, never authentication.

## Tests

`test/fleet-bus-follow-stream.test.ts` — 11 tests, all passing. Real inbox
append/read in isolated `mkdtempSync` stores: message appended after stream start;
exact-recipient filtering with checkpoint advancing past filtered rows; resume from
an emitted checkpoint without redelivery; sparse/expired cursors; backpressure
ordering (no checkpoint offered while a prior record's acceptance is pending);
injected-signal cancellation with prompt return and restored SIGINT/SIGTERM listener
counts; fail-closed on unavailable, malformed, and beyond-high-water pages;
retryable-read recovery inside the deadline; CLI argument rejection before any store
access (`bus-inbox` never created); scrubbed JSONL end-to-end through the CLI emit
seam; `--help`, `resolveFleetSubcommand`, and end-to-end `cmdFleet` dispatch through
the generated registry with a spied `process.stdout.write`.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-bus-follow-stream.test.ts` → 11/11
  pass (re-run after each state change: base fast-forward, cursor-ordering fix,
  registry + dispatch test)
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-bus-follow-stream.test.ts
  test/fleet-subcommand-registry.test.ts` → 94/94 pass; the registry sync check and
  the per-verb loader check now cover `bus-follow`
- `node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs` → regenerated the loader registry;
  `node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs --check` → exit 0
- `npx --no-install eslint src/core/fleet/bus-follow-stream.ts src/cli/fleet-bus-follow.ts
  src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts test/fleet-bus-follow-stream.test.ts` → clean,
  0 findings. Note: this worktree's `node_modules/eslint` shipped without `lib/`;
  repaired by copying `lib/` from an identical-version (9.39.5) install in a sibling
  worktree — node_modules repair only, no source changes.
- `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → exit 0, run last on the final
  tree (tsgo not installed; tsc fallback per instructions)

## Diff vs origin/master

`git status --porcelain` lists: `src/cli/fleet-bus-follow.ts`,
`src/core/fleet/bus-follow-stream.ts`, `test/fleet-bus-follow-stream.test.ts`,
`BRIDGE_NOTES.md` (new/untracked), plus the one generated change to
`src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` (+4 loader lines). Nothing committed.
Net new code ≈ 435 lines (139 core + 94 CLI + ~200 test) + 4 generated + notes.

## Limitations / notes

- A `--after` cursor above the store's high-water mark fails closed as
  `source-unavailable` (the reader returns `invalid`); resume cursors should come
  from checkpoints emitted against the same store.
- Cancellation emits no terminal checkpoint (prompt exit); the last accepted
  checkpoint remains the resume point. A final checkpoint is guaranteed only on
  ordinary duration expiry.
- The registry regeneration necessarily includes loader lines for other lanes'
  already-landed-but-unregistered verbs (`bus-scatter`, `graph-observe`,
  `graph-context-run`); without them the committed registry sync test stays red.
  They are generated one-liners, not hand edits.
- Timers in this environment run several times slow; tests drive the deadline via
  the injected `clock` seam and `vi.waitFor` on observable state, with one
  real-time expiry path retained (the retryable-reads test).
- `origin/master` advanced twice mid-session (d065640 → 4bda691 → e3b9e60, the
  second bringing the regenerated registry plus `bus-scatter`/`graph-observe`);
  the change was fast-forwarded onto it (no dependency files changed) and all
  verification re-run.
</details>

body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-REDPRFIXJOB01` (pool: devin), single commit on base `d1f3322a9`.

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-REDPRFIXJOB01

## What was built

The join between the four pieces that already existed: a fleet bridge PR whose
**newest** CI run is a completed `code` failure (not `bind-artifact` — that
class is branch-behind and never a code failure) now gets **one** fix job
dropped into the leader drop folder the ingest sweeps, instead of re-emailing
Mason on every re-run until a person writes the job by hand.

- `src/core/fleet/red-pr-fix-job.ts`
  - `selectRedFleetPrs(prs, facts)` — keeps only open PRs titled exactly
    `bridge: RQ-PHX-<id>` (jobId = the capture) that are MERGEABLE (DIRTY PRs
    belong to the recut loop) and not drafts, whose newest `facts.recent` row
    completed with conclusion `failure` and failureClass `code`. An
    in-progress newest run is skipped.
  - `fixJobId(jobId, attempt)` — strips `RQ-PHX-`, caps the stem at 34 chars,
    appends `FIX<attempt>`; result always satisfies `DROP_JOB_ID`.
  - `renderRedPrFixJob(c, fixId)` — recut-style advisory handoff: `PROMPT`
    first line, "Fix the real CI failure in ashlrai/phantom PR #N (job <id>),
    head <sha>", fetch `pull/N/head` + `FETCH_HEAD` check + apply onto fresh
    `origin/master` + fix only the reported errors, a `Reported failure`
    section (`Observed run: <runId>` marker + failed step names + ≤12 excerpt
    lines of ≤200 chars, every line scrubbed and 20+ char token runs →
    `[REDACTED]`), the recut rules block, and the `Supersedes #N`
    BRIDGE_NOTES instruction. Excerpts then step names are dropped until the
    composed file fits the writer's 8 KB cap; the body carries none of the
    denied tokens (the CODEOWNERS/`.github/` mention is phrased as
    "owner-review rules" so `validateDropJob` accepts it).
  - `runRedPrFix(opts)` — `gh pr list` (argv only) → `readCiRunFacts` →
    selection → per candidate: all five `FIX1..FIX5` ids checked via
    `dropJobExists`; an existing attempt file containing
    `Observed run: <runId>` makes the candidate `already-dropped` (never
    duplicated), the first free attempt is the fixId, all five taken is
    `attempts-exhausted`. The failed job id is found the way
    `ci-repair-packet` finds it (`…/runs/<run>/job/<id>` parsed out of the
    job's `html_url`), evidence comes from `readCiEvidence`, and the write is
    `writeDropJob(root, { lane: 'codex-personal', tier: 'work' })` only when
    `write` is set and the queued-prompt count is below
    `DROP_JOB_QUEUE_LIMIT`. Never throws: a failed read yields an empty
    candidate list with a top-level `reason`.
- `src/cli/fleet-red-fix.ts` — `cmdFleetRedFix`: `ashlr fleet red-fix [--json]
  [--hours <n>] [--write] [--runs-dir <abs>] [--repo <owner/name>]`, defaults
  24 h / dry run / ashlrai/phantom. Text output is one
  `#N <jobId> code-failure -> RQ-PHX-<fixId> (dry-run|written|skipped: …)`
  line per candidate; bad flags print usage to stderr and exit 2; reached by
  convention through the regenerated `fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` (`red-fix`).
- Tests: `src/core/fleet/red-pr-fix-job.test.ts` (selection guards, id shape,
  body contract, secret redaction, 8 KB cap, write-once + `already-dropped`
  re-run, `attempts-exhausted`, next-free-attempt, `queue-full`, never-throws)
  and `src/cli/fleet-red-fix.test.ts` (flags, dry-run/written/skipped text,
  JSON, exit codes).

## Commands run and results

- `git fetch origin master` — worktree was 10 commits behind; fast-forwarded
  to `origin/master` (143c71b7a) so `git diff --stat origin/master` shows only
  this change. No local commits exist; nothing was committed.
- `node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs` — regenerated
  `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` on the current tree (adds `red-fix`
  plus the verbs whose sources merged since the last upstream regen);
  `--check` exits 0.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config <temp config>` on the two new
  test files — **51/51 pass**. Co-located `src/**/*.test.ts` files sit
  outside the repo vitest `include` (same as the neighbouring
  `job-reissue.test.ts`), so a throwaway config with the same setupFiles was
  used and deleted afterwards.
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` (once, foreground, on the final tree):
  PASS file selection; SKIP eslint (worktree `node_modules/eslint` is pruned
  — Merge Gate lints on CI); **PASS `tsc --noEmit`**; PASS web typecheck
  (skipped — no web-ui paths); **FAIL realio lane lint** — pre-existing on
  origin/master: all five flagged files are committed `test/*.test.ts`
  fixtures not touched by this change; PASS verse sync-I/O lint.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — **exit 0**, waited for in the
  foreground as the last step (cold run takes ~30 min over ~3,147 files;
  the incremental buildinfo cache makes reruns fast).
- `git diff --stat origin/master` — lists only:
  `src/core/fleet/red-pr-fix-job.ts` (418+), `src/core/fleet/red-pr-fix-job.test.ts` (309+),
  `src/cli/fleet-red-fix.ts` (75+), `src/cli/fleet-red-fix.test.ts` (106+),
  `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` (13+).

## Dry-run against the real repo

Not possible from this sandbox: `gh` is installed but cannot read
`~/.config/gh/config.yml` (operation not permitted) and no `GH_`/`GITHUB_`
env is present, so no live `ashlr fleet red-fix` dry run was produced. The
gh-facing paths are covered by the hermetic fake runner in the tests.

## Limitations

- The verb is a manual/planner-invoked join, not a daemon: something still has
  to run `ashlr fleet red-fix --write` for drops to happen (a cron/planner
  pass or a person). Dry run is the default so it is safe to call often.
- `Observed run:` dedup is string-level over the four ingest locations; a fix
  prompt rewritten by hand loses the marker and could drop once more.
- `readCiEvidence` needs a `GitRunner`; when `opts.gh` is injected it is
  adapted to that shape (no byte-cap truncation semantics — production uses
  the real `defaultGitRunner` unchanged).
- A red PR with several failed jobs reports the first failed job's
  steps/excerpts.
- Test files are co-located per the sibling convention
  (`src/cli/fleet-ready-supply.test.ts`, `src/core/fleet/job-reissue.test.ts`)
  and therefore are not picked up by the repo vitest `include` — they run when
  named explicitly or under a scoped config, and are typechecked and linted
  with the rest of `src/`.

## Net LOC

921 insertions, 0 deletions across 5 files (4 new + regenerated registry).
</details>

body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-COSAPPROVEAPI12` (pool: claude), single commit on base `e9e50be39`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES: RQ-PHX-COSAPPROVEAPI12

## Scope change: reused the approve route that landed on master

The order was written against a tree that had no approval route. Before any code
was written, master gained #3456 (RQ-PHX-COSDESKTOPAPI11), which already ships
`POST /api/verse/fleet/cos/approve` in `src/core/verse/fleet-cos-api.ts`, mounted
under the `fleet-cos` family (`/api/verse/fleet/cos`) and documented in
`docs/COS-DESKTOP-API.md`. Adding a second approve endpoint at
`/api/verse/cos/drafts/approve`, with a different digest form and different error
codes, would have given two divergent ways to send a reply. So this job:

- adds the missing piece, a **drafts list**: `listCosDrafts` (core) and
  `GET /api/verse/fleet/cos/drafts` in the existing module;
- adds the **desktop-only refusal** (`403 COS_APPROVE_DESKTOP_ONLY` on
  `x-ashlr-channel: mobile`) to the existing approve route;
- needs **no new mount entry**: the existing `fleet-cos` prefix covers `/drafts`,
  so `workbench-types.ts` is untouched (no shared-file conflict).

Where the order and the landed route differ, the landed route's contract is kept:

| Order said | Landed (kept) |
| --- | --- |
| digest `sha256:<64hex>` | `sha256:<first 24 hex>`. The full digest never leaves the server; approve passes the full stored digest to the transport. |
| digest mismatch → `COS_DIGEST_STALE` | `409 COS_APPROVAL_STALE` |
| other channel → 409 `COS_NO_TRANSPORT` | `422 COS_NO_TRANSPORT` for `mobile`/`page`; `desktop`/`cli` origins are claim-only 200 (the reply is already on screen) |
| transport error → 502 `{ id, delivery: 'uncertain' }` | `502 { code: 'COS_DELIVERY_UNCERTAIN' }` (no error text) |
| senderId/threadId in response | omitted on the wire, matching `status`; the core `listCosDrafts` returns them |

## What changed (5 files)

- `src/core/cos/drafts.ts` (new): `listCosDrafts({ runsDir?, limit? })`. Read-only.

body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-FAILOVERREHEARSAL01SOLK3` (pool: devin), single commit on base `8bde65644`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/verse-api-mount-310.test.ts vitest.config.ts

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-FAILOVERREHEARSAL01SOLK3

## Behavior

`scripts/mac-bridge/failover_rehearsal.py` runs one bounded, reproducible
fake-host failover rehearsal through the real lease/snapshot/supervisor path.
It is not UPGRADEREHEARSAL01 (old-version state, `scripts/fleet-upgrade-rehearsal.mjs`)
and not LATESTFAILOVER01 (latest pointer selection, `latest_failover.py`).

Per invocation it:

1. creates its own `TemporaryDirectory` (prefix `failover-rehearsal-`),
2. mints fake identities `rehearsal-primary` / `rehearsal-standby` and role
   `rehearsal-leader`, builds a tiny allow-listed fake state via real
   `state_snapshot.create` + `verify_snapshot`,
3. spawns real `leader_failover.py --apply` subprocesses on a temp-local
   SQLite lease DB, each with a literal `python3 -c` dummy child that records
   its pid in start/stop marker files and exits on a quit sentinel or SIGTERM,
4. verifies the primary alone leads while the standby contends (fencing held),
5. sends SIGTERM to the primary supervisor, waits for its exit + child group
   stop + lease availability (free, standby-held, or expired past grace),
6. proves the standby launches and its restored tree matches the fake state
   (allow-listed bytes equal; unlisted paths absent),
7. prints one JSON report (`ashlr.failover-rehearsal.v1`: phase ok booleans +
   elapsed ms + outcome + takeoverMs) and exits 0 only on a full handoff;
   missing takeover, overlapping dummy children, cancellation, or deadline
   breach exit 1. `finally` terminates/reaps every descendant (quit sentinel,
   SIGTERM, escalated `leader_failover.stop_group`, orphan killpg by marker pid).

Bounds: `--deadline-seconds` 5–60 (default 25); supervisor duration runs 2s
past the deadline so the rehearsal's own clock governs. `--preview` prints the
phase plan only; there is no real-host apply mode, no path arguments, no access
to `~/.ashlr-runs`, and lease fencing is never bypassed (children see a stripped
`HOST_LEASE_CLOCK_FILE`, and the in-process status call uses `clock=time.time`).

Invocation (from CLI help epilog):

```sh
python3 scripts/mac-bridge/failover_rehearsal.py --deadline-seconds 25
python3 scripts/mac-bridge/failover_rehearsal.py --preview
```

## Measured rehearsal result (this machine, 2026-11-02)

`python3 scripts/mac-bridge/failover_rehearsal.py --deadline-seconds 25` → exit 0:

```json
{"schema":"ashlr.failover-rehearsal.v1","ok":true,"outcome":"ok",
 "deadlineSeconds":25.0,"elapsedMs":10144,
 "phases":{"snapshot":{"ok":true,"ms":4},"primaryLeader":{"ok":true,"ms":2130},
  "singleLeader":{"ok":true,"ms":615},"primaryStopped":{"ok":true,"ms":423},
  "leaseFree":{"ok":true,"ms":5482},"standbyLeader":{"ok":true,"ms":1001},
  "restoredState":{"ok":true,"ms":0}},
 "failedPhase":null,"cancelled":false,"takeoverMs":6906}
```

Takeover ~6.9s after interrupt, total ~10.1s — inside the 25s budget.

### Finding worth noting (existing code, not edited)

On macOS the `leader_failover.stop_group` post-grace `killpg(SIGKILL)` can raise
`PermissionError` when the child already exited to a zombie; it escapes the
supervisor's `finally`, so the lease release is skipped and the standby wins via
expiry+grace (~5.5s of the takeover). The rehearsal handles both paths; upstream
`leader_failover.py` was not modified.

## Commands run

```sh
HOME=$(mktemp -d) python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts/mac-bridge -p test_failover_rehearsal.py -v
python3 scripts/mac-bridge/failover_rehearsal.py --deadline-seconds 25   # RC=0 (report above)
python3 scripts/mac-bridge/failover_rehearsal.py --preview               # phase plan JSON
npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json                        # tsgo absent: npm E404
npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json                         # fallback per task; exit 0 on final rebased tree
```

## Test coverage (8 tests, all pass)

- `test_cli_handoff_succeeds` — real CLI run exits 0; all 7 phases ok.
- `test_handoff_markers_and_restored_state` — real entrypoint: both start
  markers, primary stop marker, restored `leader/VISION.md` bytes match, absent
  paths stay absent, both child pids dead, all supervisors reaped.
- `test_held_lease_blocks_and_deadline_bounds` — externally held lease →
  acquisition failure → nonzero, `failedPhase=primaryLeader`, bounded <15s,
  procs reaped (also proves the global deadline bounds a blocked phase).
- `test_failing_standby_child_nonzero_and_reaped` — standby child exits 3 →
  nonzero at `standbyLeader`, no standby marker, procs reaped.
- `test_overlap_detection_nonzero` — injected standby start marker while the
  primary still leads → outcome `overlap`, nonzero, procs reaped.
- `test_cli_sigterm_cancelled_and_tempdir_removed` — SIGTERM to the real CLI →
  nonzero, outcome `cancelled`, no `failover-rehearsal-*` dirs left.
- `test_preview_and_help_document_invocation` — preview lists phases, spawns
  nothing; `-h` shows the documented invocation.
- `test_invalid_deadline_rejected_before_spawn` — out-of-bounds deadlines are
  argparse errors before any spawn.

Tests invoke the real CLI (subprocess) and the actual `main()` orchestration
entrypoint with a non-deleting tempdir seam; no fixture-only simulation.

## Results

- unittest discover: **8 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors** (~53s).
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: **exit 0, no diagnostics** on the final
  rebased tree (tsgo package absent — npm E404 — so the `npx tsc` fallback ran
  per task instructions; an earlier attempt was killed without output mid-run
  and the re-run completed cleanly).
- Net changed LOC: **+560** (`failover_rehearsal.py` +377, test +183) — above
  the ~400 target; the seven-phase orchestration plus the required acceptance
  coverage drove it. `git diff --stat` shows only the two named files.
- No commits made; changes are uncommitted (intent-to-add only). Branch rebased
  twice onto `origin/master` (final `e377ec7a6`): upstream landed
  UPGRADERHEARSAL01 (`scripts/fleet-upgrade-rehearsal.mjs`) and
  `host_queue_ingress.py` changes — disjoint paths, no conflicts; the leased
  contracts (`host_lease.py`, `state_snapshot.py`, `leader_failover.py`) are
  unchanged.
</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-RELAYRETENTION01SOLR2

## Summary

Bounded generation retention for `scripts/mac-bridge/snapshot_relay.py`
(second-computer continuity / standby disk-fill order). The relay copied each
new generation and committed `latest.json` but never pruned, so repeated
transfers accumulated generations on the standby until the disk filled.

- New `--retain N` flag with the publisher's own bounds and default
  semantics (`snapshot_publish.MIN_RETAIN..MAX_RETAIN` = 1..64, default 3):
  the number of prior generations kept beside the selected current one.
- `relay(source, destination, apply, retain=3)` — existing three-argument
  callers preserved via a defaulted parameter. Invalid retain values
  (non-int, bool, out of range, and CLI strings) are rejected before any
  filesystem mutation; the CLI path fails via `parser.error` (exit 2).
- After an apply successfully commits a verified destination pointer,
  `snapshot_publish.prune` runs under the already-held publisher lock to
  delete surplus prior generations only. Preview mode, failed source
  verification, failed copy, failed pointer commit, and lock contention all
  leave every prior untouched.
- An already-published apply (`noop: true`) still converges retention under
  the lock without copying again.
- Pruning reuses the publisher's `generations()`/`prune()` selection: only
  generation-shaped directories carrying a valid `state_snapshot` manifest
  are victims. Symlinked entries, unrelated directories, the source store,
  and the selected current generation are never removed.

## Publication vs. retention failure reporting

Publication truth and retention truth are reported separately:

- Success: `ok: true` with `pruned: [names]` — bounded metadata (generation
  names only), alongside `copied`/`noop`/`retain`.
- Prune failure after a committed pointer: `ok: true` still reports the
  transfer truthfully (`copied`, `noop` unchanged) and adds a distinct
  `retentionError` field. The committed pointer is never rolled back and the
  copy is never denied; a later relay converges retention.

## Files changed

- `scripts/mac-bridge/snapshot_relay.py` (+49/-6): `--retain` flag and
  bounds check, `prune_retained()` helper, prune-after-commit in both the
  copy path and the noop convergence path, docstring update.
- `scripts/mac-bridge/test_snapshot_relay_retention.py` (new, 243 lines):
  11 tests over real temporary publications and real relay calls.
- `BRIDGE_NOTES.md` (this file).

Net LOC: +292 / -6 (~286 net). No changes to `snapshot_publish.py`,
existing tests, watcher files, docs indexes, `.github`, or CODEOWNERS paths.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/mac-bridge -p
  test_snapshot_relay_retention.py` — **11 tests, 11 pass** (ran twice:
  before and after fast-forwarding onto current origin/master; green both
  times).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/mac-bridge -p
  test_snapshot_relay.py` — **9 tests, 9 pass** (existing suite, unchanged,
  also re-run after the rebase).
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — `tsgo` is not
  installed in this worktree (npm 404), so the fallback ran instead.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — ran to completion in the
  foreground; **no diagnostics, exit 0**.
- `git fetch origin master`; branch fast-forwarded c3b26d304..6a5aaa211
  (upstream touched none of the edited files). Final `git diff --stat`
  contains only `snapshot_relay.py` plus the new untracked test file and
  this notes file.

## Test coverage

- 5 real publish+relay cycles with `--retain 1`: only current plus one
  prior remain; pointer still verifies; source store keeps all 5
  generations.
- Pruned names reported as bounded metadata; victim dirs actually gone.
- Noop apply converges retention (4 generations → 2) without copying.
- Preview (default and `--retain 1`) mutates nothing.
- `--retain 0`, `-1`, `65`, `abc`, bool, and non-int reject via SystemExit /
  RelayError with zero mutation.
- Injected copy failure and injected `commit_pointer` failure: prior
  pointer bytes identical, every prior generation intact; a later apply
  adopts the verified remnant and prunes.
- Held `publisher.lock` flock: relay exits 1, nothing pruned or copied;
  after release the next apply converges.
- Unrelated directory, generation-shaped dir without a manifest, a
  generation-named symlink, and a foreign symlink all survive; the symlink
  target's contents are untouched.
- Injected `prune` failure after commit: `ok: true`, `copied: true`,

  apply converges.
- `--help` advertises `--retain`.

## Limitations

- `tsgo` was absent, so typecheck ran via `tsc` fallback per the task's own
  fallback rule; it finished clean.
- Retention runs once per relay invocation; this job intentionally does not
  implement a watcher loop.
</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-MAINHEALTHROUTE02

## Summary

The desktop fleet row fetched `GET /api/verse/runs-history/main-health`, a
route no server code owned — every fetch 404'd into `notInBuild`, so
`deriveMainHealthNeedsYou` could never flag a red main. Separately, the
operator glance derived `main` from the newest `supervisor/status-*.md` by
mtime, so any later unrelated note could mask the guardian's verdict.

- `src/core/fleet/main-health-read.ts` (new): `readMainHealth({ runsDir, now })`
  reads `supervisor/status-main-guardian.md` under `$ASHLR_RUNS_DIR` (else
  `~/.ashlr-runs`) and returns exactly the `MainHealthData` wire shape the
  client validates: `v 1, generatedAt, source, statusAt, stale, guardianOff,
  red, repos[]`. Bounded read: `O_NOFOLLOW`, regular file only, 64 KiB cap,
  whole text through `scrubSecrets` before parsing. `guardianOff` is the
  `queue/MAIN_GUARDIAN_OFF` kill switch (lstat existence). `stale` is the
  status file absent while the runs dir exists, or mtime older than 3× the
  guardian interval; absent runs dir → `source 'unavailable'` + `stale
  false` (fleetless machines are not nagged). `failingCheck`/`nightlyRed`
  are clipped to 120 chars and null when they carry a home path; `fixJobs`
  keeps only `/^RQ-[A-Z0-9-]{3,60}$/` ids. Unparseable content yields
  `state 'unknown'`, never `'green'`.
- `src/core/verse/main-health-api.ts` (new): `createMainHealthApi` serves
  GET on the pinned path; other methods 405, unknown query params 400
  `VERSE_INVALID` (same posture as runs-history-api.ts), other paths
  decline so the next module runs. A thrown reader answers 200 with
  `source 'unavailable'`, like lane-truth. Read-only.
- `src/core/verse/verse-api.ts`: added `'main-health'` to
  `MountedApiModuleId` and mounted it directly after `'runs-history'` —
  runs-history-api.ts exact-matches its three paths and declines this one.
- `src/core/fleet/operator-glance-read.ts`: `readOperatorGlance` consults
  `readMainHealth` first. When the guardian status was actually read
  (`source 'ok'` + `statusAt` set): `red > 0` → `down`; fresh + non-empty +
  all-green → `up`; stale/partly-unknown/empty → `unknown`. When no
  readable guardian status exists it falls back to the newest
  `supervisor/status-*.md` text exactly as before, so the existing glance
  tests are untouched.
- `test/verse-api-mount-310.test.ts`: pinned mount list and the
  `Record<MountedApiModuleId, string>` representative map name
  `'main-health'` — a mechanical accommodation the mandated mount-table
  change requires; no assertion weakened.
- `test/main-health-route-02.test.ts` (new): fixture status file → route →
  200 body → `mainHealthQuery.fetch` (stubbed fetch) → `{ kind:
  'available' }` → `deriveMainHealthNeedsYou` urgent item; absent status →
  stale; absent runs dir → unavailable + not stale; `MAIN_GUARDIAN_OFF` →
  `guardianOff`; POST → 405; unknown param → 400; home-path failing-check
  never reaches the response; glance `down` for red guardian + newer
  unrelated status file; stale green guardian never reads `up`; fresh
  all-green → `up`; no guardian file → status-file fallback.

## Guardian status layout caveat

`~/.ashlr-runs/` is TCC-protected: `ls`, `find`, and direct file reads all
return `Operation not permitted` even after a scope grant, so the real
`status-main-guardian.md` could not be inspected. What is knowable from
outside: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.ashlr.main-guardian.plist` runs
`/usr/local/bin/python3 ~/.ashlr-runs/bin/main-guardian.py` with
`StartInterval` **300** seconds (5 min), logging under `~/.ashlr-runs/
guardian/` (`launchd.out`, `launchd.err`); the needs-you UI already names
`queue/MAIN_GUARDIAN_OFF` as the kill switch and `guardian/guardian.log` as
the log. The parser is therefore tolerant rather than format-frozen:
`key=value`/`key: value` fields, `name@branch` tokens, markdown table rows
(with a declared header row), and bare `name … state` lines all feed one
`MainHealthRepo`; a repo claim needs corroborating signals before the first
token counts as a name; anything unreadable is `unknown`, never `green`;
interval lines (`interval:`, `every N <unit>`) set the staleness threshold —
otherwise 30 minutes per the task spec (the real 5-minute plist cadence
means a dead guardian can take up to 90 min to flag stale if the file does
not state its interval). No real values were copied into code or fixtures.

## Companion-job search

No `RQ-PHX-MAINHEALTHREAD01` branch exists on the fork
(`git ls-remote`); `gh` is unauthenticated in this sandbox so PR search
could not run. The nearest branch, `codex-bridge/RQ-PHX-MAINHEALTHROW01`,
carries only the already-merged web-ui side (#2785). The server half was
built here from spec.

- `npm ci` — the worktree's eslint install was incomplete (`lib/` absent)
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/main-health-route-02.test.ts` —

  test/verse-api-mount-310.test.ts` — 36/36 pass; combined re-run
  47/47 pass
- `npx eslint <all six touched files>` — clean, exit 0
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — exit 0
- `git diff --stat origin/master` — only the planned files (the three new
  files are untracked, so they appear in `git status` rather than
  `--stat`)

Per instructions, `npm run lint` / `npm run typecheck` were not run;
`verify-changed.mjs` was not run.

## Net LOC

+661 −5 (new files 640 + tracked-file edits ≈21 insertions / 5 deletions;
`git diff --numstat origin/master` shows 21/5 for tracked files). Slightly
over the ~400-line target because the tolerant per-repo parser carries
table/kv/positional handling — all in the one new reader file.

## Limits / notes

- Nothing committed; all changes uncommitted in the worktree.
- `test/verse-api-mount-310.test.ts` was edited beyond the listed files —
  unavoidable: it pins the mount-table id list verbatim, and the spec

- The real status-file layout remains unverified (TCC). If the guardian

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE NOTES: RQ-PHX-RECOVERYFOLLOWSTOP03SOOG1

## Summary
Added `--stop-file <path>` option to `fleet-apps-follow` verb, enabling operator-accessible graceful stop detection without killing the process.

## Behavior

### `--stop-file <path>`
- **Pre-existing stop file**: Before the first reader call, checks for stop file presence via `readFileSync`. If found, returns a JSONL summary with `reason: "stopped"`, `delivered: 0`, `nextCursor: <current checkpoint cursor>`, without calling the reader. Exits 0.
- **During idle wait**: Checks stop file between reads and during idle sleep (bounded polling, 100ms slices). Exits promptly when detected, respecting existing duration deadline and AbortSignal.
- **Checkpoint preservation**: On stop, the current cursor is preserved in the selected checkpoint (if any). The stop file itself is NOT deleted or modified.
- **Error handling**: If the stop file exists but is unreadable (permission denied), reports explicit error to stderr, never falsely claims clean stop, and emits summary with `reason: "stopped"`.
- **Distinguishability**: `reason: "stopped"` is distinct from existing reasons (`deadline`, `event_limit`, `cancelled`, `invocation_finished`, `unavailable`, `invalid_cursor`).
- **No file contents**: The stop file content is never printed or echoed.

## Files Changed

### `src/cli/fleet-apps-follow.ts` (21 insertions, 51 deletions relative to origin/master)
- Added `--stop-file` to CLI argument parsing (arg validation, no existing flags affected)
- Added `readFileSync` import (replaces unused `existsSync`)

- `lastJsonObject` returns the last complete JSON object in stdout.
- On a parse failure, the fail detail now includes the first 200 chars of stdout after the shared `scrubSecrets` filter from src/core/util/scrub.ts (unchanged) plus the smoke sentinel replacement. If the scrubber can't load, the snippet is withheld rather than printed raw.
- New test in test/companion-workflow-smoke.test.ts covers noisy stdout, no-object input, and that the snippet never carries the sentinel or a GitHub token shape.

title: bridge: RQ-DAEMONTICK-UNBLOCK
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-DAEMONTICK-UNBLOCK` (pool: devin), single commit on base `fcf6309ab`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** src/core/daemon/loop.ts src/core/fleet/tick-hooks-live.ts test/m201.daemon-loop.test.ts

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-DAEMONTICK-UNBLOCK — bridge notes

## Summary

The resident daemon tick can no longer freeze `lastTickAt`. Every awaited
stage of `tick()` runs inside a bounded phase (`runTickPhase` in
`src/core/daemon/tick-phases.ts`): deadline + `AbortSignal` + exception
capture + degrade/timeout status + a durable ledger entry. `runDaemon` wraps
each `tick()` in a 60-minute backstop (`DAEMON_TICK_DEADLINE_MS`,
`opts.tickDeadlineMs` overrides) and persists
`lastTickAt`/`lastTickOutcome`/`lastTickPhases`/`lastTickError` in a
`finally` — so a thrown, timed-out, or still-open tick always advances the
heartbeat. A tick abandoned at the deadline is parked; the loop refuses a
second tick while it stays open (`refused-open`) and clears when it settles.

Phase ledger: `{name, status, durationMs, error?}` on `DaemonTick.phases` and
`DaemonState.lastTickPhases` (codec is additive/tolerant — old state files
parse unchanged, malformed rows drop). `phm daemon status --json` exposes
`.tick = { lastTickAt, outcome, lastError, phases[] }`; `tickInProgress` still
names the live stage. `--budget` start output now reads "legacy --budget
metered cap … (metered USD spend only)" — it gates metered USD only.

Bounded phases added (defaults): `tick hooks` 26 min (wraps
`boundedBeforeTick`), `mirror-prep` = prep deadline + abort grace + 30 s
(inside `tick-hooks-live.ts` `beforeTick`; mirrors.ts internals untouched —
RQ-APPDIAG-1-LANESTALE owns them), `backlog-refresh` 5 min, `self-heal` /
`ancillary` / `auto-merge` / `proposal-repair` 5 min, `invent` 3 min,
`reflection` 3 min, `capacity` + `capacity-recheck` 30 s, `dispatch-plan`
60 s, `dispatch-hook` 60 s, `dispatch` = worst-case serial turn count ×
(turn watchdog + grace).

Dispatch: `superviseFleetTurn` bounds EVERY turn at
`localFleet.taskTimeoutMs` — fleet-armed turns keep the abort-own-controller
watchdog; non-fleet turns are left detached under their own engine
backstops (`turn-deadline` outcome) so a long frontier run is never cut. A
dispatch phase that exceeds its bound gives queued items explicit
`dispatch-deadline` outcomes; admitted runs continue detached.

Invent probes `resolvePlanningClient` under a 30 s bound; `null` records
`skipped: no-frontier`, a wedged probe records `timeout`/`degraded` — never
an await that outlives the tick.

Child-process audit (AMEND 01:20): `runVerifySubprocessAsync` already had
hard timeout + SIGTERM/SIGINT→SIGKILL process-group kill; the phase
`AbortSignal` now flows into it (self-heal/reflection/invent/playbook paths
take `opts.signal`). `log stream` watchers are file-polled and never
awaited for exit (3 s ready / 3 s barrier bounds). Unbounded `which`/`where`
PATH probes on the tick path (`engines.ts`, `orchestrator.ts`,
`model-manager.ts`) gained `timeout: 2_000`.

`runTickPhase` also keeps the `phm daemon status` live-progress contract: it
notes the phase name while running and restores the prior stage label on
settle only when its own name is still the last write (same pop semantics as
the maintenance pass), so newer tick/phase labels and stop-settled labels are
never overwritten.

## Files

- NEW `src/core/daemon/tick-phases.ts` (303 LOC) — phase runner + ledger +
  outcome derivation.
- NEW `test/daemon-tick-unblock.test.ts` (624 LOC) — 20 regression tests.
- NEW `docs/daemon-tick-phases.md` (124 LOC) — operator reference.
- `src/core/daemon/loop.ts` — phase funnel wiring, `runBoundedDaemonTick` +
  guaranteed persistence, `superviseFleetTurn` all-turn bound, dispatch pool
  bounds, signal propagation, `hooks`/`tickDeadlineMs` seams.
- `src/core/daemon/state.ts`, `src/core/types/daemon.ts` — additive fields +
  tolerant codec.
- `src/cli/daemon.ts` — `.tick` JSON block + `--budget` relabel.
- `src/core/fleet/{self-heal,tick-hooks-live}.ts`,
  `src/core/generative/invent-cycle.ts`, `src/core/learn/{reflect,playbooks}.ts`
  — `AbortSignal` propagation.
- `src/core/run/{engines,orchestrator,model-manager}.ts` — bounded PATH probes.
- `test/m201.daemon-loop.test.ts` — two assertions updated for the deliberate
  `runSelfHealCycleForRepos(repos, cfg, opts)` third-arg (asserts the phase
  signal arrives).
- `docs/contracts/CONTRACT-M24.md`, `docs/llms.txt`, `docs/README.md`,
  `AGENTS.md` — contract + index entries.

Net LOC: +830 / −116 tracked; +1051 in new files (303 + 624 + 124).

## Commands run

- `npm ci` — repaired incomplete `node_modules` in this fresh worktree
  (eslint's `lib/` was missing; 403 packages, 0 vulnerabilities).
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — PASS (file selection, eslint changed
  files, tsgo --noEmit, realio lane, verse sync-I/O). Pre-existing real-io
  membership warnings on unchanged files only.
- `npm run check:docs` — PASS (`ok: true, errors: []`).
- `npm run typecheck` — backend `tsc --noEmit` PASS. `typecheck:web` FAILS on
  185 pre-existing errors in `src/web-ui/**` test files — all baseline, none
  in touched paths (verified: 0 errors under `src/core`, `src/cli`, `test/`).
- `npm run lint` — FAILS on the pre-existing baseline (57 errors:
  `debug-31b3.mjs`, tracked `.js` files, `vitest.minimal.mjs` parse error,
  etc.). Zero errors in touched files (eslint changed-files PASS above).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/daemon-tick-unblock.test.ts` —
  20/20 PASS.
- `test/m24.loop.test.ts` 50/50, `test/m24.state.test.ts` 68/68,
  `test/m537.daemon-tick-authority-capability.test.ts` 2/2,
  `test/daemon-cli-310b.test.ts` 24/24, `test/daemon-liveness-310b.test.ts`
  10/10, `test/m490.daemon-state-recovery-cli.test.ts` 3/3,
  `test/daemon-state-resolution-clock.test.ts` 2/2,
  `test/m501.daemon-state-resolution.test.ts` 31/31,
  `test/m486.daemon-spend-durability.test.ts` 13/13,
  `test/m406.daemon-stop-quiescence.test.ts` 2/2,
  `test/m487.daemon-state-quarantine.test.ts` 60/60 (one 5 s timeout flake in
  the loaded parallel run; passes in isolation),
  `test/verse-daemon-pause.test.ts` PASS, `test/doc-facts.test.ts` 6/6.
- `test/m201.daemon-loop.test.ts` — first full run 279/288 (9 regressions:
  6 tick-progress labels leaked by phase notes, 2 self-heal call-arity
  assertions, 1 env-blocked EPERM takeover). Fixed via pop-on-exit label
  restore in `runTickPhase` + updated call-arity assertions. Final full run:
  **286/288** — the only failures are the two environment cases below.

## Environment limitations (pre-existing, not caused by this change)

- `/bin/ps` is sandbox-blocked here (`Operation not permitted`), so
  `verifiedProcessStartRef` cannot prove pid identity. Two real-io cases fail
  environmentally and reproduce on the unmodified main checkout:
  - `daemon-first-tick-314` "an abort (tick deadline / shutdown) cancels the
    install and kills its group"
  - `m201.daemon-loop` E5e "EPERM resident pid reused … is taken over"
- `outcome-daemon-loop.test.ts` — 12 fixture-setup failures
  (`ResourceNativeProfilePrepareError`) reproduce identically on the main
  checkout; sandboxed tmp dirs fail `inspectPrivateDirectory`.
- `test/m487` "checks expiry immediately before no-clobber receipt
  publication" hit the 5 s test timeout once under parallel load; passes
  isolated (3.2 s).
- `m201` `A1h5b3b-ordinary-crash` (15 s limit): passed at 8.6 s in the first
  full run; later runs time out at 21–33 s as this host's real-io slowed.
  Verified NOT a regression — the test times out identically on the
  completely clean tree (git stash) at 21.7 s.
- `m201` `E5e` — needs `verifiedProcessStartRef` pid-reuse proof; `/bin/ps`
  is seatbelt-blocked here so takeover stays fail-closed. Environmental.

Not done: no commit, no push, no tag, no publish — all changes uncommitted
in this worktree.
</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-GUARDIANCOMMANDREACH02

## Goal
Serve Mason's Nov 1 23:31 always-on main-guardian order: make the already-merged
guardian `compact` and `retry` maintenance commands reachable through the real
fleet command registry, so agents can actually maintain guardian state.

## Problem
`src/cli/fleet-guardian-compact.ts` exported a const-arrow with an obsolete
comment claiming the registry generator must not collect it. The generator
(`scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs`) only collects `export async function
cmdFleet<Name>(...)`, so `fleet guardian-compact` fell through to
"unknown fleet subcommand". `guardian-retry` already exported the conventional
async function but was absent from the committed registry.

## Exact paths changed
- `src/cli/fleet-guardian-compact.ts` — `export const = async () =>` converted
  to `export async function cmdFleetGuardianCompact(args, compact = compactGuardianState): Promise<number>`;
  injection seam, parser, exit codes (0/1/2) and bounded output unchanged;
  obsolete const-arrow comment removed. (+2/-5)
- `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` — regenerated with the existing
  generator (`node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs`); adds only the
  `guardian-compact` loader line on top of fresh origin/master. No generator
  redesign, no dispatch changes. (+1)
- `test/fleet-guardian-command-reach-02.test.ts` — NEW regression (9 tests,
  +~127 lines). Uses temp dirs/invalid args only; never touches real guardian
  state, the host, or model endpoints.

## Registry reconciliation
Work started on `8bd6977f3`; before finishing, origin/master was re-fetched
(16b5c5c43). Master had meanwhile added `guardian-retry` (registry regeneration
by another worker) plus new verbs `lane-merges` and `self-tick`. The branch was
fast-forwarded to `16b5c5c43`, the stash-popped registry conflict was resolved
by rebuilding the registry from the fresh tree with the same generator, so
upstream verbs are preserved and only `guardian-compact` is added.
`node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs --check` exits 0 on the final tree.

## Regression coverage (acceptance mapping)
1. Loader reachability: for both `guardian-compact` and `guardian-retry`,
   `FLEET_SUBCOMMAND_LOADERS[verb]()` resolves and the loaded module exposes
   the conventional export name from `resolveFleetSubcommand` with matching
   function `.name`.
2. No unknown-command fall-through: `cmdFleet(['guardian-compact'])` → exit 2
   `invalid guardian-compact arguments`; `cmdFleet(['guardian-retry'])` →
   exit 3 validation; bad flags reach each parser (exit 2). All assert stderr
   never contains `unknown fleet subcommand`.
3. Generator persistence proof (not a hand-maintained list): the existing
   `generateFleetRegistry` is run against an isolated CLI fixture directory
   containing a byte copy of the real `src/cli/fleet-guardian-compact.ts`;
   the generated fixture registry includes the `guardian-compact` loader.
4. Compact's original validation via its real loaded export: malformed temp
   manifest → exit 1, bad flag → exit 2, output file never materialized,
   source state byte-identical.
5. Real-tree `generateFleetRegistry(['--check'])` === 0.

## Checks run (all pass/fail counts)
- `node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs --check` → exit 0 (final tree).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-guardian-command-reach-02.test.ts`
  → 1 file, 9/9 passed (re-run after the master fast-forward: 9/9).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-guardian-compact-02solu2.test.ts
  test/fleet-guardian-retry-02solu1.test.ts` → 2 files, 8/8 passed (confirms the
  signature change kept the existing behavior contract).
- `npx eslint src/cli/fleet-guardian-compact.ts
  src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts test/fleet-guardian-command-reach-02.test.ts`
  → exit 0, no warnings.
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → tsgo absent in this
  worktree; fell back to `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → exit 0.
  No unrelated failures observed; the full-project typecheck is green.

## Net LOC
3 insertions + 5 deletions across 2 source files; +1 new test file (~127
lines); BRIDGE_NOTES.md. Total well under the 400-line cap, one concern.

## Environment note / limitation
This fresh worktree shipped with a partially extracted `node_modules/eslint`
(missing `lib/`). Repaired by copying the identical eslint 9.39.5 package from
sibling worktree `RQ-PHX-GUARDIANRETRYEXEC02` (package.json verified identical);
no dependencies were installed or upgraded from the network. `pnpm-lock.yaml`,
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `package.json` changed upstream (RQ-PNPM-GVS) but are
untouched here.

## Constraints honored
Did not commit/push; did not touch `.github/**` or CODEOWNERS-protected paths
(checked `origin/master:.github/CODEOWNERS` — no match for the three paths);
did not read `~/.codex`; did not modify `fleet.ts`, `index.ts`,
`completions.ts`, `help.ts`, docs indexes, `scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs`,
`fleet-subcommand-resolve.ts` or `fleet-guardian-retry.ts`; Security GATES v3,
hold list, privacy and billing rules untouched. No new secrets, no external
messages.
</details>

body:

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-VERIFY-DEDUPE

## Summary

`scripts/verify-changed.mjs` now dedupes on already-passed states. Before any
check it fingerprints the working state and exits 0 with
`SKIP verify-changed` when that exact state previously passed; on a full pass
it records a marker so repeats are free.

- `workingTreeHash(root)` produces a real git tree hash of the working state:
  the live index is copied to a private `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `git add -A` stages
  committed + staged + unstaged + untracked non-ignored content, and
  `git write-tree` emits the hash (~0.5s on this repo; the real index is never
  touched).
- `verifyDedupeInput` keys a marker on `{ tree, base (merge-base vs
  origin/master), eslint+typescript installed versions, tsgo presence, node
  version, platform }` — the base matters because changed-file selection and
  realio scoping depend on it, and checker drift can change a verdict on an
  identical tree.
- `verifyDedupeKey` = sha256 over the JSON input record.
- Markers live at `<git-common-dir>/phantom-verify-passed/<key>.json` —
  shared across all worktrees — written atomically via temp+rename, pruned to
  the newest 256 (`VERIFY_PASSED_CAP`), with `PHANTOM_VERIFY_PASSED_DIR` as a
  relocation override. Corrupt markers count as misses.
- Bypass flag kept: `--force` argv or truthy `PHANTOM_VERIFY_FORCE` reruns
  verify (a forced pass still records). Fingerprint failure (e.g. no
  `origin/master`) degrades to a warn + normal run; nothing is recorded on
  failure.

Docs updated: `docs/verify-changed.md` (dedupe section, new env vars, --force),
`CONTRIBUTING.md` (command table + paragraph), `AGENTS.md` (worker note).
`test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs` gained the new suite's membership.

- `test/verify-changed-dedupe.test.ts` (new): 13/13 pass — unit coverage of

# Planner execution bridge

Based on origin/master 7a6dab9fe, fetched and fast-forwarded before edits. Current master has a core planner-run.ts but no fleet planner CLI. The existing selector is reused unchanged; this command reads every configured candidate's health from its own runs root.

`ashlr fleet planner run --config /absolute/config.json --prompt-file /absolute/prompt [--json]` launches exactly one eligible candidate, preserving priority, argv, cwd and binary prompt stdin. Required timeoutMs is 1..3600000. JSON reports provider, status, actual child exitCode (null for spawn errors), and selection reason/next reset when all exhausted. No retry follows launch. Timeout and cancellation kill the child and wait for close. Child output is discarded to avoid sensitive diagnostics. Config/validation errors expose only a fixed error message.

The launch follows the existing planner runner's foreground shell:false convention and ORCH_OFF hold. It additionally refuses PAUSE, HOLD, QUEUE_DISABLE, OPUS_LEADER_OFF and unavailable switch state. Existing candidate runs roots must be readable owned directories. No holds are changed. No queue message, auth file or environment dump is read. Explicit CODEX_HOME cannot point into ~/.codex, including resolved aliases; other input paths are also checked. Without explicit CODEX_HOME the child receives the explicitly configured runsRoot; the command creates no login directory or auth state. Configure a working login explicitly for Codex.

Fake example configuration (all paths and provider names are placeholders):

```json
{
  "timeoutMs": 120000,
  "candidates": [
    {"provider":"fake-primary","executable":"/tmp/fake-tools/primary","argv":["planner"],"cwd":"/tmp/fake-work","runsRoot":"/tmp/fake-primary-runs","CODEX_HOME":"/tmp/fake-login-primary"},

}
```

```sh
ashlr fleet planner run --config /tmp/fake-planner.json --prompt-file /tmp/fake-prompt.txt --json
```

title: bridge: RQ-SWE-DESKPARITY-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE-DESKPARITY-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `6778b16f0`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/verse-workbench-contracts-310.test.ts

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE-DESKPARITY-1

## Gap chosen

**The Files pane was a registry stub.** `docs/VERSE.md` said it plainly: "a
simple list of folders and touched files, not a file browser yet." Every
comparable agent desktop (Devin, Claude Code, Codex, Grok) ships a real file
explorer with preview. Phantom had everything else in the parity list —
live session status, diffs/PR review, run/stop, approvals, notifications,
queue, settings, usage/budget — but no way to look at the project tree.

This change makes the Files pane a real, read-only file browser:

- `POST /api/verse/files/browse {sessionId, root?, path?}` — one directory
  listing (≤256 entries), lazy per-directory.
- `POST /api/verse/files/read {sessionId, root?, path}` — a bounded UTF-8
  text preview (≤64 KiB, `truncated` flag when larger).

Both are POSTs inside the existing `session-controls` family, so they inherit
the workbench dispatch gate and the mutation token — browsing is a
*privileged read*: the pane shows an unlock row until the token is held, and
no file content ever reaches a model ("Add to message" quotes only the
`@path`, same as the touched-files rows).

## Alternatives considered

- **Per-chat usage/budget strip** — already covered: the usage surfaces and
  budget API exist; marginal gain.
- **Transcript search** — Sources/Reasoning panes and session search already
  cover retrieval; lower leverage than a missing whole surface.
- **Terminal/browser/diff polish** — all already at parity or beyond.
- **Full file *editor*** — editing, search-in-file, image previews are
  explicitly out of scope (documented in `docs/VERSE.md` known limits);
  read+preview is the coherent PR-sized slice.

## Implementation summary

Backend (`src/core/verse/`):

- `session-files.ts` (new, ~320 lines): async browse/read over the chat's
  own `verseSessionRoots`, each root re-validated per request by
  `checkWorkspaceRootPathAsync`. Containment is proven by realpath
  (`physicalPathAsync` + `isUnderPath`); a requested `root` must physical-
  match one of the chat's roots. Names are policy-filtered (no dotfiles but
  a small safe set, no credential/key/build-output names, strict UTF-8,
  no control chars). Listings are capped at 256 dirents (over-cap is a
  `LIMIT` 413, not silent truncation), directories-first sorted, entry stats
  fanned out at concurrency 8, and vanished/unreadable entries are skipped.
  Reads use `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, require a regular file owned by
  this uid, read at most 64 KiB, re-lstat the path against the opened
  dev/ino, re-prove containment, and reject non-UTF-8/control-byte content.
  Directory inode is re-verified after enumeration (lstat→opendir swap).
- `session-controls-api.ts`: `handleFilesReadRoute` validates bodies
  strictly (unknown keys → 400), maps `SessionFilesError` to
  `VERSE_INVALID`/400, `VERSE_FILE_NOT_FOUND`/404, `VERSE_FILE_LIMIT`/413,
  `VERSE_FILE_UNAVAILABLE`/503. `handleFiles` keeps GET = fuzzy finder and
  accepts only the exact POST browse/read paths.
- `workbench-types.ts`: route constants + request/response contracts.
  No digest field — a bare sha256 is secret-shaped to `sanitizePublicJson`
  and nothing consumes it; `sizeBytes`/`byteLength`/`truncated`/`path`
  already identify the snapshot.

Frontend (`src/web-ui/routes/verse/panes/builtin/`):
